original_question: Use the work of Humphries and Khan to compute weight-aspect upper bounds for the sixth moment of L(1/2, f tensor g) when f and g vary over primitive forms of level 1 and weights k and ell, under the conditions |k - ell| = O(1) and K < k + ell <= 2K.
target_in_paper: Open Problem (15) in the Problems section: use Humphries-Khan [42] to compute weight-aspect upper bounds for the sixth moment of L(1/2, f ⊗ g) when f and g run over primitive level-1 forms of weights k and ell with |k-ell| = O(1) and K < k + ell ≤ 2K.
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper and is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Problem (15). It correctly identifies Humphries-Khan as the intended input, asks for weight-aspect upper bounds, targets the sixth moment of L(1/2, f ⊗ g), keeps the family to primitive forms of level 1, and includes the same near-equal-weight and dyadic conditions |k-ell| = O(1) and K < k + ell ≤ 2K.
missing_details: The paper's exact target is an open problem in the problem list, not a theorem or conjecture.
The ambient automorphic setting should be made explicit: f and g are primitive holomorphic Hecke eigenforms/newforms for the full modular group SL_2(Z), i.e. level 1 over Q.
A stand-alone version should introduce notation for the families, such as H_k^*(1) and H_ell^*(1).
The weights k and ell should be specified as even integers; otherwise the family is not completely described.
The phrase sixth moment should be written as an explicit sum or average over pairs (f, g); Problem (15) leaves the summation notation implicit.
The Rankin-Selberg convolution L(s, f ⊗ g) should be named explicitly, and the sixth power should be written explicitly, typically as |L(1/2, f ⊗ g)|^6.

The averaging/normalization is not stated in Problem (15): the paper does not say whether the moment is a raw count or a harmonic/Petersson-weighted sum. Nearby Problems (11) and (13) use harmonic normalization via L(1, ad f), so this ambiguity must be fixed in any fully stand-alone formulation.
The O(1) condition should be quantified as a fixed constant C independent of K with |k-ell| ≤ C.
The asymptotic regime K -> infinity and the intended uniformity of implied constants should be stated.
The dyadic restriction is on k + ell, not separately on k and ell, and this should be made explicit.
The paper does not specify a target exponent or optimal bound, so a faithful rewrite should ask for an explicit upper bound in K rather than build in a stronger claim not stated there.
refined_question: Let H_k^*(1) denote the set of primitive holomorphic Hecke eigenforms of level 1 and weight k, and fix a constant C > 0. Using the methods of Humphries-Khan [42], determine an explicit upper bound, as K -> infinity, for the dyadic weight-aspect sixth moment M_6(K) := sum_{substack{k, ell in 2N, K < k + ell <= 2K, |k-ell| <= C}} sum_{f in H_k^*(1)} sum_{g in H_ell^*(1)} |L(1/2, f ⊗ g)|^6, where L(s, f ⊗ g) is the Rankin-Selberg convolution of f and g.
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Problem (15), and your draft already tracks it very closely. The paper does not provide extra notation for the family in Problem (15), so the main refinement needed is to make the family of primitive level-1 holomorphic forms and the Rankin-Selberg central values explicit. The most important hidden ambiguity is the averaging measure: Problem (15) itself does not specify whether the sixth moment should be raw or harmonically weighted, even though nearby Hecke-form moment problems in the same paper are written with harmonic normalization. Reference [42] identifies the intended Humphries-Khan input.
